open: In the name of Allah. Assalamu alaikum, my dears. Come closer, tonight’s story is very beautiful.
s1a: Noah… Ilyas… do you remember? I promised you an important question. At the end of his life, the Prophet Yaqub called his sons and asked them: “What will you worship after me?”
s1b: And what did they say, Grandma?
s1c: That, I will tell you at the end of the story. Snuggle up nicely… Today I’ll tell you about the Prophet Yaqub, peace be upon him. He was the son of Ishaq and the grandson of Ibrahim.
s2a: Do you remember? The angels told Sara: after Ishaq comes Yaqub. And so it was. Ishaq was blessed with a son named Yaqub, and Allah made him a prophet too. Yaqub and his family lived in the desert.
x_s2a: Imagine with me this wide, quiet place… where a noble prophet lived who loved Allah very much.
s2b: And what did Yaqub teach his children?
s2c: The most important thing in the world! Ibrahim had advised his sons to it, and Yaqub said the same words to his sons: “O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims.” That means: stay with Allah, your whole life long.
x_s2c: That means: we love Allah and obey Him, every single day.
s3a: Yaqub was a strong prophet. In the Quran, Allah described him as one of “those of strength and vision”, which means: strong in doing good, and seeing the truth clearly. He prayed, did good, and guided people to Allah. Yaqub had many children, and one of them was named Yusuf.
s3b: One day, little Yusuf came to his father and said: “O my father, indeed I have seen eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me!”
s3c: Eleven stars? What does that mean?
s3d: Yaqub was wise, and he understood that this vision was something great. He said: “O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers or they will contrive against you a plan.” And he told him: Allah will choose you, teach you, and complete His favour upon you, as He completed it upon your forefathers Ibrahim and Ishaq.
x_s3d: See how gently Yaqub advised his son… A wise father loves his children and protects them.
s4a: Then came a hard day. The brothers said to their father: Send Yusuf with us tomorrow! At first, Yaqub did not want to, then he let him go. In the evening, the brothers came back without Yusuf. They were crying and saying: The wolf took him! And they brought Yusuf’s shirt.
s4b: Oh Allah! And did Yaqub believe them?
s4c: No. Yaqub said: “Rather, your souls have enticed you to something”, which means: you made up this story. Then he said words we will never forget: “So patience is most fitting. And Allah is the one sought for help.”
s4d: Beautiful patience means: we are patient, and we don’t complain to people. And everything in our hearts, we tell to Allah.
x_s4d: For example: if one day you feel sad, don’t get angry and don’t shout… instead, say: O my Lord, help me.
s5a: Many years passed, and Yaqub never forgot Yusuf. He grieved for him so much that his eyes became white from grief. His sons said to him: Will you always keep remembering Yusuf?
s5b: Yaqub said: “I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah that which you do not know.” Then he said: O my children, go and look for Yusuf, “and despair not of relief from Allah”!
s5d: That, my dear, is a big story all of its own. I’ll tell it to you next time!
s6a: And now, the question I promised you. When Yaqub grew very old and the end of his life drew near, he called his sons and asked them: “What will you worship after me?” They said: “We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim and Ismail and Ishaq, one God. And we are Muslims in submission to Him.”
x_s6a: What a beautiful answer! They all said: we worship Allah alone.
s6b: Wait, Grandma… Ismail was Yaqub’s uncle, not his father!
s6c: Well done, my dear, you paid close attention! Arabs sometimes call an uncle “father”, because he is so close to the family. And look: Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqub and his sons, all of them worshipped the One God, Allah.
s7a: Oh… they’ve fallen asleep. My dears… when you feel sad, remember Yaqub: be beautifully patient, and tell Allah everything that troubles you. Never despair of Allah’s mercy. And stay with Allah, your whole life long.
s7b: Next time, I’ll tell you about Yusuf… about a well, a prison and a king. And you, watching us right now: if you liked the story, ask your parents to subscribe to our channel, so you don’t miss the next story.
close: And you, dear fathers and mothers: subscribe to our channel, and share these stories with the people you love, so that together we pass on the beautiful message of Islam to our children.
final: Good night, my dears. I entrust you to Allah, with whom nothing entrusted is ever lost.
